title: Pala succession and Bengal intervention
text: The end of the local Pala line and the extent of Bengal intervention are unsettled. Tingyadeva appears in the later Kamauli account as the ruler whose disaffection prompted replacement. Do not treat c.1110–1126 as dated epigraphic reign bounds.

title: Vaidyadeva’s appointment and grant
who: Vaidyadeva, appointed by Kumarapala of Bengal
text: Kamauli records his replacement of Tingyadeva and a grant from Hamsakonci. It locates Kamarupa-mandala within Pragjyotisa-bhukti. Absolute dating is disputed:1123 and1142 occur in scholarship. Hamsakonci is unlocated here; Kamauli near Varanasi is the discovery place, not his Assam capital.

title: Rulers known through Vallabhadeva’s genealogy
text: This is an ancestral sequence in a later record, not proof of three consecutively dated reigns across all Kamarupa. Relations to Vaidyadeva and the exact extent of their domains remain uncertain.

title: Vallabhadeva’s charitable endowment
text: The Assam plates record a food-distribution establishment near a Siva temple east of Kirtipur in Hapyacha-mandala, endowed at his father’s command. The editor permits1184/1185. These places are not securely identified; a Tezpur find region is not a kingdom boundary.

title: Bakhtiyar Khalji’s failed expedition and return
who: Unnamed Kamarupa ruler(s); Prithu identification disputed
text: The Tibet expedition ended in a disastrous retreat. Kanai-Barashi-Bowa commemorates destruction of the invading Turks but does not name the defender. Prithu/Britu in Persian narratives has disputed identification, including an Awadh interpretation; no1187–1228 reign or Bhitargarh capital is treated as established.

title: Iwaz’s pressure and the Gachtal evidence
who: Visvasundaradeva attested in scholarship; unnamed regional rulers
text: Iwaz’s eastern campaigns and tribute claims belong to this context. Gachtal’s stone record is read as Saka1149/1227 and associated with Visvasundara and temple repairs. Equating him with Prithu is disputed. Iwaz’s death is conventionally1227, not1228. Succession and any brief Delhi-imposed tributary arrangement remain uncertain.

title: Samudrapala at Ambari
text: The Ambari inscription supplies a1232 attestation, not a c.1100 reign. It mentions a royal-associated sattra at Yogihati. The king’s genealogy, accession, end of reign and full territory are not established. This display window is not an18-year reign.

title: Sandhya and the western reorganisation
who: Sandhya, conventionally the Rai of Kamrup
text: Historians associate Sandhya with Kamarupanagara and the transition to Kamata. His accession and earlier genealogy are uncertain; do not extend his reign backward to1229 as a settled fact.

title: Yuzbak defeated; transition toward Kamata
text: Yuzbak’s1257 invasion ended in defeat and death during the retreat. The victory is attributed to Sandhya in the historical reconstruction. The move from Kamarupanagara to Kamatapur is usually placed after this, around1260; it is not a securely dated same-day consequence.
